findings.rule: Incident date must fall within the policy period; the tier at the incident date must cover the peril (COMP covers own damage; collision is a covered event).
findings.explanation: The incident date of 2026-06-16 is within the period 2025-11-01 to 2026-10-31. The COMP tier covers own damage, and a collision with an object (guardrail) is a covered event under 2.1. The incident was in Australia and the premium was paid. The supplied clauses contain no waiting period or territory rule, and nothing in the facts suggests the cover check fails. The licence exclusion override is outside the scope of this area.

findings.rule: A claim must be notified within 30 calendar days of the incident date; later notification needs an explanation (31-90 days) or an approved clause 2.3 exception (beyond 90 days).
findings.calculation: days_incident_to_fnol = 1, which is within the 30 calendar day window. No late-notification exception is needed.
findings.explanation: The claim was notified 1 day after the incident, within the 30-day window in clause 2.1. Clauses 2.2 and 2.3 are not triggered.

findings.rule: Licence expired by 30 days or less, driver otherwise eligible, renewed within 30 days of incident, not suspended or cancelled: rebuttable exclusion 3.4 may be set aside with Level 3 approval and a file note identifying the rebuttal condition; dual approval (second at L3+) required. Other exclusions (vehicle use, registration, alcohol/drugs, unlisted driver) checked.

evidence.value: Driver's licence expired 29 May 2026 (18 days before the incident) and was renewed 25 June 2026 (9 days after). Licence was not suspended or cancelled; driver otherwise eligible. Rebuttal under POL-MTR-002 3.4 applied; exclusion set aside by L3 with L4 second approval. Renewal confirmation on file.

findings.calculation: Expired 18 days <= 30; renewed 9 days after incident <= 30; expired not suspended/cancelled; L3 approver meets 4.3; second approver L4 meets 3.1(d).
findings.explanation: The licence exclusion was engaged but the rebuttal conditions were all met, and the override was approved by L3 with an L4 second approver and a file note recording the condition. The override was of a rebuttable exclusion, not an absolute one. No other exclusion applies: use was private as declared, registration was current, the driver was the listed policyholder, and no alcohol reading was recorded.

findings.rule: Tracks are tested in order; first met is assigned. Triage within 1 business day. Claim assigned STANDARD: SIU not triggered (score 0, no referral trigger), not Complex (value under 50,000, no injury, liability clear, no total loss), not Fast-track (claimed 6,900 exceeds 5,000).
findings.calculation: Order 1 SIU: score 0 < 60, no trigger. Order 2 Complex: 6,900 <= 50,000, no injury, liability clear, no total loss. Order 3 Fast-track: 6,900 > 5,000 so not met. Order 4 Standard applies. Triage took 1 business day, within the 1 business day limit.
findings.explanation: Standard is the correct track under the precedence rules, and triage was completed within 1 business day of lodgement. No re-triage boundary was crossed, as the value never fell within the fast-track limit.

findings.rule: Clause 4.1 requires an assessment for all claims except fast-track claims where photos suffice. It does not say whether a desktop assessment satisfies that requirement on a STANDARD track claim. Clause 4.2 sets timeframes only for field assessments, and none are supplied for desktop assessments. The rule on which assessment type is acceptable is missing.
findings.explanation: An assessment was done (desktop, 2026-06-23). The supplied clauses do not say whether a desktop assessment is adequate for a standard-track claim, so this cannot be confirmed as compliant or breached. Clause 4.2's 3 and 10 business day limits apply only to field assessments, so they cannot be tested. Needs human review.

findings.rule: Clause 4.3 requires an independent external assessor above AUD 100,000. Clause 4.4 requires a second assessment on a written dispute, a variance above the greater of 30% or AUD 20,000, or a conflict of interest. Clause 4.5 requires an assessment to be no more than 90 days old at the settlement decision.
findings.calculation: Variance = (6900 - 6600) / 6900 = 4.3%, which is below 30%. The AUD 20,000 limb is not reached either. Assessment age is 3 days, which is within 90 days. The claim value of 6,900 is below 100,000.
findings.explanation: No external assessor was required and no second assessment was triggered. The assessment was not stale at the decision date.

findings.rule: Missing rule: the supplied clauses contain no authority level limits (monetary settlement limits per level), so whether L3 approver authority covers a total incurred cost of AUD 5,800 cannot be confirmed. Dual approval is required under 3.1(d) where a rebuttable exclusion is set aside; that requirement appears met on its face (L3 first approver, L4 second approver). Independence of approvers under 3.2 and the recording of identities, roles and timestamps under 3.3 cannot be verified because only levels are recorded.
findings.explanation: Dual approval is triggered by 3.1(d) and a second approver at L4 is recorded, satisfying the level requirement. A single payment of 5,800 equals total incurred, so there is no payment splitting under 2.2. However, the per-level monetary limits are not in the supplied clauses, so L3 authority cannot be confirmed. Approver identities, timestamps and reporting lines are also not in the claim facts. Separately, whether the exclusion in POL-MTR-002 3.4 was validly rebutted is a cover/exclusions matter outside this authority review, and POL-MTR-002 was not supplied.

findings.rule: Fraud score is the sum of triggered indicator points; a score of 0-29 is Low and requires normal handling. No mandatory referral triggers under 5.1 apply.
findings.explanation: No fraud indicators are recorded, so the score of 0 is correct and falls in the Low band. Normal handling applies, and no SIU referral, enhanced verification or block was required. The 5.1 triggers are not met: no indicators are triggered and the claimed value is far below AUD 250,000. The licence exclusion override is outside the fraud area.

findings.rule: Required decision-stage and settlement-stage documents must be on file before the decision; exception/rebuttal evidence required where relied on.
findings.explanation: Required codes: CLAIM_FORM, ID_VERIFIED, DRIVER_LICENCE (driver in control), PHOTOS, REPAIR_QUOTE_ACCREDITED, ASSESSMENT_REPORT, BANK_VERIFIED (payment) and EXCEPTION_EVIDENCE (rebuttal relied on). All are on file, and documents were complete on 2026-06-25, before the 2026-06-26 decision. Not required: TP_DETAILS, CTP_REFERENCE, LICENCE_VERIFIED (claim not over AUD 10,000), GST_DECLARATION (not GST registered), total-loss documents. The documentation area is not breached. Whether the rebuttal itself was valid is outside this area.

findings.rule: Acknowledgement within 2 business days of lodgement; decision within 20 business days of docs-complete (standard track) and within 4 months of lodgement; decision communicated within 5 business days; payment within 10 business days of acceptance; status updates at least every 20 business days.
findings.explanation: Acknowledgement took 1 business day (limit 2). Standard-track decision was 1 business day after docs complete (limit 20) and within the 4-month cap. Decision was communicated in 0 business days (limit 5). Payment was 2 business days after acceptance (limit 10). The maximum contact gap was 3 business days (limit 20; the claimant is not vulnerable). All service timeframes were met.

findings.rule: Excess and net settlement: basic excess plus any additional excess (young/inexperienced driver 3.4(a)/(b), unlisted driver 3.4(d)) is deducted from gross settlement; no ITC for non-GST-registered claimant; not a total loss.
findings.calculation: Additional excess: driver aged 52 (not under 25), full licence 34 years (not under 2), driver listed NA so none. Expected excess = 800. Net = 6600 - 800 - 0 ITC = 5800, matches net_paid 5800 and payments_total 5800.
findings.explanation: Excess, ITC (none, claimant not GST registered), and net payment are correct. Not a total loss and no recovery applies. The exclusion override on licence status is outside the settlement area and not assessed here.
